messages:
Marta: heads-up — customer reporting inconsistent embedding vector sizes between Hosted and Dedicated for the same model (open-embed-lite-v1). Seen both 512 and 768 dims from different endpoints. Repro steps attached.
Alex: ugh. do we have any recent model-variant changes or alias remaps?
Marta: customer runs: hosted -> POST /v1/embeddings model=open-embed-lite-v1 -> returns 768. dedicated pool -> same model name -> returns 512. They say they didn't change client code.
Devon: can we confirm the dedicated runtime is actually loading the same weights? Maybe we're falling back to an older quantized variant.
Priya: tagging infra: @Devon can you check model manifest mapping in dedicated cluster? also any recent autoupdate?
SRE Bot: Deploy event: dedicated-cluster-3 pulled artifact open-embed-lite-v1@sha256:abc123 at 2026-02-28T08:12:03Z.
Alex: that sha256 matches the hosted one in model-catalog?
Marta: hosted manifest shows open-embed-lite-v1@sha256:abc123 too. so they claim same artifact.
Devon: hmm. different runtime config could change postprocessing. Do embeddings get truncated or padded by batching logic?
Priya: customer mentioned they batch 32 inputs for dedicated but send single requests to hosted. batching could be exposing a bug in the KV cache / prefix handling.
Marta: repro from customer:
```
# hosted (single)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HOSTED_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-lite-v1","input":["hello world"]}'
# returns: {
#  "data": [[... 768 floats ...]]
# }
# dedicated (batch of 32)
curl -X POST https://dedicated.redwood.local/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEDICATED_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-lite-v1","input":["hello world","...", ...]}'
# returns first vector length 512
```
Devon: that snippet is really useful. can we get the exact JSON lengths & a small sample of the vector (first 8 floats) to fingerprint?
Marta: provided: hosted first 8 floats: [0.012, -0.21, 0.003, ...] length=768. dedicated first 8 floats: [0.012, -0.21, 0.003, ...] length=512. values align for first 256 elements, then dedicated stops.
Alex: oh — values align up to a point. suggests truncation not model change. maybe batching path slices sequence dims?
Devon: I remember a batching optimization we merged: continuous-batch-packing that reinterprets token-dim vs embedding-dim when the model uses custom output heads. If a shape mismatch happens, it might pack fewer dims into the buffer.
Priya: any recent flags toggled on dedicated but not hosted? e.g., `--enable-fast-batch` or `embedding-truncate-on-oom=true`?
SRE Bot: Config snapshot dedicated-cluster-3 at 2026-03-02T02:03:11Z: --enable-fast-batch=true, --embedding-slice-size=512.
Alex: there's the smoking gun. hosted doesn't have `--embedding-slice-size` set (default=768).
Marta: customer says they didn't change anything server-side. they expect parity. we need action plan.
Devon: short fix: set dedicated cluster to default slice size 768 and roll. Long-term: we should make slice-size automatic or fail loudly on mismatch. This is a regression risk for mixed-deploy customers.
Priya: agree. also need to check whether private deployments might have different defaults; customer uses Private for region failover and reported intermittent 512s from that endpoint too.
Alex: ops: schedule a canary config change on dedicated-cluster-3: set --embedding-slice-size=768, restart worker on 3 nodes, validate sample responses.
Marta: can you also draft a repro checklist for the customer so they can confirm in their environment? include token check, batching size, sample vectors and lengths.
Devon: repro checklist: 1) single request to hosted & capture vector length and first 8 floats. 2) batched request to dedicated & capture lengths/first 8 floats. 3) run `curl` with explicit `Content-Type: application/json` and POST a minimal batch of 2 inputs to prove truncation. 4) collect server logs `redwood-runtime` for `embedding-slice` messages. 5) include `X-Request-Id` headers.
Marta: customer also flagged billing discrepancy — they got charged double for embedding units on dedicated during repeat retries. Could be retry loop because the dedicated endpoint returned 200 but vector length inconsistent and client retried with different params.
Alex: file a billing support ticket to freeze invoicing for that account while we investigate. @SupportBot can you create billing hold?
SupportBot: creating billing hold for account cust-98765. Ticket: BH-2026-134. Notified finance. :white_check_mark:
Priya: security note — private envs sometimes have stale tokens in env var mounts. the customer reported a 401 previously; that's likely separate but worth confirming their ded/private keys map to the same model access tier.
Marta: action items:
- Devon: revert/adjust `--embedding-slice-size` on dedicated and coord with infra (ETA 1h).
- Alex: run regression on hosted to ensure we don't introduce perf regressions (ETA 2h).
- Priya: reach out to customer with repro checklist + ask for X-Request-Id and sample vectors (ETA 30m).
- SupportBot: create billing hold & notify finance (done).
Devon: updating cluster config now. patch: `--embedding-slice-size=768` -> rolling restart. I'll post logs when done.
SRE Bot: Rolling restart initiated on dedicated-cluster-3 at 2026-03-03T14:21:10Z.
Devon: restarted node-1. sample test result against dedicated after node-1: vector len=768 for single and batched size 8. looks good so far.
Marta: customer confirms they see 768 on dedicated for small batch. they will run larger throughput tests later.
Alex: note for engineering backlog: add an explicit parity check in deploy pipeline that validates embedding dims across hosted/dedicated/private after model rollouts. file a ticket.
Priya: logging improvement: when `--embedding-slice-size` differs from model expected output dims, emit WARN with fingerprint to help debugging.
Marta: thanks everyone. I'll keep thread updated if customer regresses during throughput tests. :heart:
SupportBot: thread closed for now but will reopen if customer reports new mismatch.
